venues.architect: Pedro Ramírez Vázquez and Rafael Mijares Alcérreca
venues.primary_tenant: Club América; Mexico national football team
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (hybrid / GrassMaster reinforced) with deep drainage. NOTE: 'underground thermal control' claimed in the original sheet is NOT SPECIFIED IN any cited authoritative source and has been removed.
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Project cost reported at ~2 billion Mexican pesos (~€110 million) per StadiumDB. Separately, ESPN reports a financing stack of ~3.6 billion pesos (~$180M USD): ~1.5 billion pesos (~$75M) already invested by operator Ollamani plus a ~2.1 billion peso (~$105M) Banorte loan repayable over 12 years (verified against ESPN). Some 2026 grass-feature coverage cites a round '~$150M USD' total — a third non-reconcilable figure. These describe different things (project cost vs. financing raised vs. rounded total) and are not reconcilable from cited sources; treat as approximate/attributed, not a single confirmed total spend.

venues.architect: Concept design: Jean-Marie Massaud & Daniel Pouzet; Sports architects: Populous (formerly HOK Sport); Architect of record: VFO Architects
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass — high-quality grass installed/renewed to FIFA standards in the 2025 WC2026 renovation (StadiumDB). The venue's original 2010 artificial turf was replaced with natural grass in 2012 (Wikipedia). NOTE: the 'hybrid / ~95% natural / FIFA-Pro-certified / Mexico's first hybrid' characterization is NOT supported by any cited source and was removed.
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Over MXN 250 million (over US$12.4 million) — StadiumDB, Mar 2025. This is the WC2026 upgrade cost, distinct from original construction cost. USD figure is an approximate conversion per StadiumDB.

venues.architect: Populous with VFO (Federico Velasco, lead designer)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (hybrid; aggregator sources describe a GrassMaster-type system with under-turf ventilation — exact natural/synthetic split and drainage mechanism NOT SPECIFIED IN AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES)

venues.architect: Studio Phillips Barratt (original); Stantec Architecture (2011 retractable-roof revitalization)
venues.primary_tenant: Vancouver Whitecaps FC (MLS) and BC Lions (CFL)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (hybrid sod), custom Kentucky bluegrass / perennial ryegrass blend grown in the Fraser Valley; installed over BC Place's normal FieldTurf synthetic surface for the tournament
venues.renovation_cost_2026: PavCo estimates BC Place upgrades plus World Cup operating costs at CA$171 million–CA$181 million; the broader province/city hosting-cost estimate is CA$483 million–CA$581 million (net projected cost CA$100M–CA$145M after revenue). No single isolated 'renovation only' figure is confirmed across sources; the 2026-05-12 BC government release explicitly declined to disclose upgrade-specific dollar amounts ('within the capital budget estimate shown in Budget 2026').

venues.architect: Brisbin Brooks Beynon Architects (BBB Architects); Gensler (2014–2016 expansion)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass — SISGrass hybrid (Kentucky bluegrass reinforced with stitched synthetic fibres); FIFA-standard pitch installed during Phase 2 renovations (Dec 2025–Mar 2026)
venues.renovation_cost_2026: CA$157.9 million final cost (CA$132.9M from City of Toronto + CA$25M from MLSE), per City of Toronto completion release (2026-03-24). Initial March 2025 announcement budgeted CA$146M (CA$123M City + CA$23M MLSE); the very first 2024 plan was a CA$37M temporary-seating contract.

venues.architect: 360 Architecture (HOK), tvsdesign, Goode Van Slyke Architecture, Stanley Beaman & Sears
venues.primary_tenant: Atlanta Falcons (NFL) and Atlanta United FC (MLS)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass hybrid (natural grass interwoven with synthetic fibers; ryegrass/Kentucky bluegrass mix grown for the indoor venue), over a rebuilt sub-surface with new sand layer, irrigation and aeration; replaces the stadium's permanent FieldTurf CORE artificial surface
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Approximately US$200 million staged upgrade program for Mercedes-Benz Stadium reported ahead of the World Cup (per StadiumDB and aggregated reporting), described as multi-year work not fully completed until summer 2026; this figure is an estimate for the broader upgrade program and is NOT cleanly isolated to WC2026-specific work in cited sources

venues.primary_tenant: New England Patriots (NFL); New England Revolution (MLS)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (ryegrass / Kentucky bluegrass sod) — artificial FieldTurf CORE torn out and converted to grass for the World Cup
venues.renovation_cost_2026: NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCES (no cost figure for the WC2026-specific grass/seating work was published in cited sources; a separate $250M stadium renovation completed in fall 2023 predates and is unrelated to FIFA requirements)

venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (Kentucky bluegrass and ryegrass blend, sod-grown in Colorado and trucked to Arlington; installed on a raised temporary platform with underground irrigation, ventilation/temperature control and retractable grow lights) — replacing the stadium's normal artificial turf
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Approximately $295 million (WFAA/StadiumDB reporting; ESPN reports a reported total close to $300 million). Covers the broader World Cup reconfiguration — raising/re-orienting the field and seating, natural-grass pitch system, and interior/facility upgrades — not the grass alone. Reported/estimated figure; exact audited total NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCES.

venues.architect: Populous (HOK Sport) with Houston Stadium Consultants (Architect-of-Record; joint venture of Lockwood, Andrews & Newnam and Hermes Architects)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (temporary modular pitch) — approx. 81,000 sq ft of grass grown in Colorado, installed indoors over a shallow Permavoid water-storage/drainage cell system on the stadium's concrete floor, replacing the permanent Hellas Matrix synthetic turf for the tournament
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Two distinct figures, NOT to be conflated: (1) approx. US$15 million in World Cup-specific NRG Stadium upgrades, paid by Houston's World Cup host committee, per a Harris County-Houston Sports Authority spokesperson (Houston Public Media, Jan 2025) — the source itself hedges this as "about $15 million" (estimate). (2) A separate US$55 million Capital Improvement Project (CIP) approved Nov 2025 by the Harris County Sports & Convention Corp. covering NRG Stadium, NRG Center and NRG Arena infrastructure broadly (not solely World Cup pitch work).

venues.architect: Kivett and Myers (original 1972); Populous/HOK Sport (2007–2010 renovation)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass — NorthBridge Bermudagrass (hybrid), resodded for 2026 with a SubAir-style sub-surface air/ventilation and vacuum-drainage system installed beneath the pitch (drains storm water; pumps chilled air to the grass roots in extreme heat)
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Missouri allocated US$50M (May 2023), of which $42.5M is for Arrowhead Stadium World Cup prep (the other $7.5M to the KC2026 nonprofit for FIFA contractual obligations); $19.6M spent across the first two of five phases as of mid-2026, with ~$23.5M budgeted for the final three phases (per KSHB, June 2026). Turner Construction received >$17.1M and Populous >$1.73M as construction administrator.

natural grass (Bermuda; FIFA mandates natural grass; venue already uses Tifway 419 Bermuda and staged 2024 Copa America and 2025 Club World Cup on grass)
venues.renovation_cost_2026: NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCES (no dedicated WC2026 renovation budget figure found in cited authoritative sources; venue already has natural grass and required no major capacity/structural rebuild)

venues.city: East Rutherford, New Jersey (New York/New Jersey metro)
venues.architect: 360 Architecture (lead); EwingCole (per Wikipedia rev 1360702806, listed alongside Rockwell Group and Bruce Mau Design)
venues.primary_tenant: New York Giants and New York Jets (NFL)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (Bermudagrass) installed on modular trays over existing FieldTurf infrastructure; sand base, irrigation, and ventilation layers topped by ~600 rolls of turf to form a 105 x 68 m FIFA pitch. Converted from artificial turf specifically for the World Cup; Bermudagrass first installed early May 2026 (per ESPN).
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Over US$100 million in World Cup-readiness upgrades, privately funded by Giants/Jets ownership, on top of the original ~US$1.6 billion construction cost; per meetstadium.com (single outlet, not an itemized/FIFA-audited figure).

venues.primary_tenant: Philadelphia Eagles (NFL); also Temple Owls (NCAA football)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass — Kentucky bluegrass and perennial ryegrass blend knitted with HERO Hybrid Grass fibre, mowed to 22mm per FIFA spec (replacing the regular hybrid surface)
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Under USD $10 million for all stadium modifications (executive estimate, 'final costs still being worked out'), per Philadelphia host-city executive Meg Kane (Billy Penn, May 2026); costs shared by the Philadelphia Eagles, the Philadelphia host committee and FIFA.

venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (hybrid) — natural turf reinforced with stitched-in synthetic fibres for FIFA consistency/durability; FIFA-spec surface installed for the 2026 World Cup (reported installed March 2026)
venues.renovation_cost_2026: Contested / not a single agreed figure. Two distinct sourced numbers exist: (1) a $120 million package (49ers borrowed/invested via the NFL stadium fund, reported 2023) targeting premium-seating remodels and new 4K video scoreboards ahead of the 2025 season [KNBR/StadiumDB]; (2) a broader "$200 million" total renovation figure cited for the venue's 2025-2026 upgrades preparing it to host both Super Bowl LX and the World Cup [Yardbarker]. The $200M is a press characterization of overall investment, not an itemized World-Cup-specific cost. World-Cup-specific pitch-conversion cost is NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCES.

venues.primary_tenant: Seattle Seahawks (NFL); Seattle Sounders FC (MLS); Seattle Reign FC (NWSL)
venues.field_type_2026: Natural grass (stitched/hybrid: natural grass woven with synthetic fibers, grown in Moses Lake, WA), temporarily installed over the stadium's FieldTurf CORE for the tournament
venues.renovation_cost_2026: USD 19.4 million in Washington state capital-budget funding approved by Gov. Bob Ferguson for the World Cup upgrades (Seattle DJC headlines it as a "$19M World Cup upgrade")
